newsitem.title: UK: GOLF-PARNEVIK SEIZES OPEN LEAD, WOODS SHOOTS 64.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-PARNEVIK SEIZES OPEN LEAD, WOODS SHOOTS 64.

text.p: Jesper Parnevik, seeking to atone for thowing away the 1994 title, overhauled Darren Clarke with a five-under-par third-round 66 on Saturday to lead the British Open by two shots.
The 32-year-old U.S.-based Swede fired a two-under-par 33 on the back nine to turn a four-shot deficit with nine holes left into a two-stroke lead oorthern Irishman.
"I birdied the first two holes and felt like I could do whatever I wanted on the golf course," the Swede said.
"My thought was to get into the lead for tomorrow. All I'm going for is a win."
Parnevik was beaten by Nick Price by one shot in the 1994 Open at Turnberry when he bogeyed the last hole.
Clarke, the joint first-round leader and two ahead overnight, slid to a 39 on the back nine with four bogeys in a level-par 71.

Americans Fred Couples and Justin Leonard stood five shots off the lead, Couples after a one-under-par 70 comprised of 16 pars, an eagle two with a 168-yard six-iron shot at the 11th and a bogey at 17.
Leonard shot 72 with 15 pars, two bogeys and a birdie at 17.
World number one Tiger Woods, the U.S. Masters champion, shot a 64 that matched the record round for British Opens at Royal Troon.

The 21-year-old American phenomenon was joint eighth, eight shots off the lead, and Parnevik for one could not imagine Woods would be a factor "unless he gets a good start and the wind blows 80 miles an hour".
Parnevik holed from 12 and 20 feet at one and two, dropped a shot at the short fifth after missing the green, then birdied six and the seventh from 16 feet.
He birdied the 10th from 15 feet but missed the 12th green with his approach to take bogey. Then he birdied the long 16th with a sand wedge third to six feet.
A superb three iron to three feet at the demanding 223-yard 17th capped his round.
"I saw Darren dropping a few on the back nine so I decided to go for it on 17.
"It was important to put pressure on Darren because when you're three or four ahead you can free-wheel a bit. I knew if I could make a few birdies coming in I could put pressure on him."
He lost in 1994 through not looking at the scoreboard. "I think I'll be looking at them tomorrow," he said.
Clarke shot his third successive four-under 32 on the front nine but this time had four bogeys on the back nine and the one at 13 could have been worse.
He pushed his drive into dense rough, came out straight left into rough so heavy he had to take a penalty drop from an unplayable lie before holing from six feet for the bogey.
Clarke said he made mistakes and bad club selections on the back nine.
"It's disappointing to come back in the manner I did, but I am in the last group. I have a chance to win the Open tomorrow and hopefully if the chance presents itself I will take it," he said.

Woods followed a superb front nine with a fabulous finish as he beat up the 7,079-yard course that had resisted him for two rounds to match the Troon Open course record of 64 set by Greg Norman in the final round in 1989, when par was 72.

His 64 was one shot outside the Open record of 63 achieved seven times. Though the wind was benign, Woods negotiated the tough back nine in 32, three under par, including an eagle three at the 542-yard 16th with a 15-footer and a spectacular holed chip shot from down a bank for birdie at the short 16th.
He bumped his second shot into the side of the bank to kill its pace and watched as it rolled onto the green and curled into the cup.
He said he had aimed for a spot on the bank three inches from where his ball hit before bouncing onto the green.
Then he saved par from a greenside bunker at the last.
Earlier Woods had flirted with disaster at the same 11th hole where he took a triple bogey seven on Thursday.
This time, after taking two shots to escape the gorse, he got away with a bogey five.
"The bogey at 11 kept me going but I can go lower. I had two bogeys. I just have to eliminate the bogeys."
